title: Grow in Faith and Heed God's Witnesses
summary_text: Peter writes to those who share faith through the righteousness of Jesus Christ, their God and Savior. God's power and promises give what they need for life and godliness, so they must grow in faith, love, and other good traits. This growth makes their calling and election sure, and Peter wants them to remember it after his coming death. He saw Christ's glory and heard the Father honor His Son. The prophets' word is also a sure light, since they spoke from God as the Holy Spirit moved them.
key_points: God's power and promises enable believers to share in the divine nature and escape corruption caused by evil desires.
Growth in faith, godliness, and love makes believers fruitful and confirms their calling and election as they enter Christ's eternal kingdom.
Peter expects to die soon and works to keep these truths in his readers' memory after his departure.
Peter witnessed Christ's glory and heard the heavenly voice identify Him as the Father's beloved Son.
The prophets' word shines like a lamp; prophecy comes from God through speakers carried by the Holy Spirit.

title: False Teachers Face Destruction for Their Deceit
summary_text: Peter warns that false teachers will deny the Master who bought them, use lies for profit, and bring ruin on themselves. God's past judgment shows that He rescues the godly but punishes the unrighteous. These teachers seek adultery and money, follow Balaam's path of wickedness, and lure others into sin through desires of the flesh. They promise freedom while trapped as slaves to evil. Those who know Jesus Christ and the way of righteousness but turn back to evil end worse off than before.
key_points: False teachers will deny their Master, spread destructive teachings, and exploit believers through greed and lies.
God judged angels and ungodly communities but preserved Noah and righteous Lot, showing His power to rescue and punish.
The teachers despise authority and pursue adultery and greed, following Balaam's path of wickedness.
They promise freedom but remain slaves to corruption, luring others through desires of the flesh.
Those who know Christ and then return to corruption reject the holy commandment and end in a worse condition.

title: The Lord's Patience and the Coming Day
summary_text: Peter recalls the prophets and apostles, then warns of scoffers who doubt the Lord's promised coming. They ignore God's creation and the flood, though His word now holds the world for judgment by fire and the ruin of the ungodly. His delay gives time for repentance, but His day will come without warning. Believers must live in holiness and godliness as they await the new heaven and earth where righteousness lives. Peter warns against twisting Scripture, including Paul's letters, and urges growth in Christ's grace and knowledge.
key_points: Scoffers question the promised coming while ignoring God's earlier creation and judgment by water.
God's sense of time differs from human measures, and His patience allows repentance rather than destruction.
The Lord's day will come unexpectedly with fiery destruction, calling for holiness while believers await a new creation filled with righteousness.
Believers must seek peace and blameless lives, recognizing the Lord's patience as salvation rather than twisting Scripture as unstable people do.
Peter warns against lawless error and calls for growth in Christ's grace and knowledge.
